mismatch.message: With acoustics disabled, the hidden metal-eating monster adds a crunch message in JS before the sewer rat bite; C suppresses the hearing line.

summary: The admitted v54 baseline matches 862/863 screens and all RNG/cursor entries before the first screen difference at segment 0, step 634. The case uses !acoustics. C mon.c:meatmetal reaches its offscreen, verbose object-consumption branch and calls You_hear("a crunching sound."); pline.c:You_hear suppresses the phrase when acoustics are disabled. JS mon.js:meatmetal emits the literal hearing message through monsterMessage, so the top line becomes “You hear a crunching sound.  The sewer rat bites!” instead of “The sewer rat bites!”. A fresh replay after syncing accepted Main c5187612 reproduces this at the same step with identical RNG and cursor streams.

source.branch: In meatmetal(), after an eligible metallic object is selected, cansee(mtmp->mx, mtmp->my) is false and flags.verbose is true. C emits Soundeffect and delegates the text to You_hear("a crunching sound."), which applies deafness, underwater, unaware, and acoustics rules. JS enters the matching branch but sends the literal line directly through monsterMessage, bypassing those rules.
callers: monmove.c:postmov() calls meatmetal(mtmp) for metallivorous monsters after movement and treats return value 2 as death; the selected recorded turn follows this production monster-movement path.
dependencies: pline.c:You_hear() is already ported as youHear() in js/pline.js and re-exported through js/monmove.js; it returns null when acoustics is disabled and provides the source hearing prefixes for other states. No return-valued unported callee is needed for the text fix.
The adjacent C Soundeffect call is a sound backend effect, not the recorded top-line discrepancy; preserve its existing handling and make no claim that the sound backend was newly ported.

nethack-c/upstream/src/mon.c:meatmetal() (1463-1531), specifically the offscreen verbose branch at 1508-1514, calls You_hear("a crunching sound."). nethack-c/upstream/src/pline.c:You_hear() (436-451) applies deafness and flags.acoustics. js/mon.js:meatmetal() (1579 onward) currently emits a literal through monsterMessage instead.

nethack-c/upstream/src/monmove.c:postmov() (1665-1668) is the production caller for metallivorous monsters and checks meatmetal() == 2. js/monmove.js already wires the existing meatmetal owner and preserves the result check; the missing behavior is the C hearing gate within meatmetal.
